Represents unusual bullous variant, hence atypical. Closest vocabulary terms are erythematous papulovesicles and clear thin-walled vesicles; bullae proposed as not in vocabulary.

panels.rationale: Single-panel clinical photograph of an infant's trunk and arm showing an erythematous papular eruption. The caption explicitly identifies it as miliaria rubra, a configured target disease, and the in-text mention confirms miliaria rubra on the face, arms and chest. The finding matches the erythematous papulovesicles of miliaria rubra. Skin is adequately lit and appears light (Fitzpatrick I–II). The patient is an infant (head circumference 35 cm, active), mapped to age_group child. No third-party copyright indicated. [raw subtype: miliaria rubra]

panels.rationale: H&E histology from a case report of bullous miliaria showing intraepidermal edema (spongiosis) consistent with the disease; article title and in-text confirm biopsy from miliaria lesions. [raw subtype: bullous miliaria]

panels.figure_caption: Intraepidermal edema separating the epidermal collagen fibers (H&E, 20×). H&E: hematoxylin and eosin
in_text_mentions: A 4 mm skin punch biopsy was obtained from the abdominal lesions for further characterization of the nature of the skin lesions and to assist in making the diagnosis. Hematoxylin and eosin staining of the epidermis revealed hyperkeratosis, focal parakeratosis, spongiosis, and exocytosis of lymphocytes and neutrophils. The dermis showed moderate perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate without eosinophils or neutrophils. Histopathological evidence of vasculitis or viral infection was absent (Figure 5).
